scraped.scraped_description: Master copies of the DISARM frameworks, with generated files to help you explore the data - DISARMFoundation/DISARMframeworks

name: DISARM Frameworks
tagline: Master copies of the DISARM disinformation TTP frameworks for describing and countering disinformation incidents
sdg_alignment: SDG 16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
dependency_risks: relies on volunteer community for updates
Blue Framework contains TTPs from authoritarian contexts requiring contextual caution

policy_outcomes.description: Tested in trials with NATO disinformation units
Tested in trials with EU disinformation units
Bundled with MISP (threat sharing platform) for operational use by ISAOs

outcome_methodology: Framework adoption and integration into operational platforms (NATO, EU, MISP); no formal impact evaluation published
documented_limitations: Blue Framework includes TTPs observed in authoritarian contexts — companion guide advises caution
each user must assess ethical/legal appropriateness of countermeasures independently
failure_modes: framework may lag emerging disinformation tactics
misuse of Blue Framework TTPs in non-democratic contexts
curation_criteria: Red Framework: creator TTPs from observed incidents; Blue Framework: countermeasures from 2019 volunteer workshop
contributor_governance: Open contributions via Google Form; DISARM Foundation holds design authority
community_ownership: Community-driven; CC-BY-4.0 licensed; DISARM Foundation as steward
controversies: Blue Framework includes tactics from authoritarian governments, requiring explicit user caution per documentation
ai_involvement: No AI/machine learning components; framework is taxonomy-based and human-curated
political_relevance_summary: DISARM Frameworks addresses civic technology. Master copies of the DISARM disinformation TTP frameworks for describing and countering disinformation incidents.

movement_building_utility.notes: Provides technical infrastructure that other civic tools or services build upon.

generalizability_notes: Highly generalizable; already deployed across multiple countries. Open-source codebase facilitates replication.
